study.research_problem: Additively manufactured metallic lattices offer controllable porosity and stiffness, but the in-vivo bone response depends on manufacturing, lattice topology, pore geometry, material state, animal model, and implantation time. The field lacks a consistent biological interpretation of bone maturation, interior ingrowth, and fixation across these conditions.
study.exact_gap: Prior reviews emphasized materials, processing, mechanical properties, or surface modification; this review instead maps in-vivo histological and histomorphometric responses. It finds no systematic, condition-matched evidence that identifies an optimum pore architecture, pore size, porosity, or unit cell for osseointegration in a critical-sized defect.
study.objective_or_hypothesis: Survey in-vivo studies of additively manufactured metallic porous implants, classify fabrication and lattice architectures, and synthesize histological, histomorphometric, and mechanical-proxy trends while exposing animal-model and measurement heterogeneity.
study.study_design: Narrative review with quantitative table extraction from cited preclinical in-vivo studies; the authors synthesize published histology/histomorphometry and do not perform a new animal experiment or pooled meta-analysis.
study.sample_or_model: Reviewed studies used murine, leporine, canine, caprine, ovine, porcine, and other preclinical models with titanium, Ti-6Al-4V, tantalum, iron-manganese, and related porous implants produced mainly by powder-bed AM. The review reports study-level ranges rather than one pooled sample.
comparators: Reticulated, stochastic, TPMS, functionally graded, micromachined, and other lattice architectures
Pore sizes from roughly 50 to >1000 micrometres, varied strut thickness, and porosity from 30% to 83.5%
Commercially pure titanium/Ti-6Al-4V versus tantalum or iron-manganese and solid controls
Outer versus inner lattice regions and different histomorphometric segmentation schemes
Different animal species, anatomical sites, implantation times, and critical-sized defects
method_spine: Summarize SLM, EBM, SLS, DMLS, and directed-energy deposition limitations and the materials represented in in-vivo studies.
Classify reticulated, stochastic, TPMS, functionally graded, and other architectures and relate strut/unit-cell changes to nominal pore size, porosity, transport, and mechanical response.
Contrast species, defect size, implantation time, woven-to-lamellar maturation, fibrosis, and bone penetration.
Define BV/TV, BA, BIC, pull-out, push-out, and removal torque, while highlighting inconsistent inner/outer segmentation.
Synthesize conditional pore/porosity trends and state that the apparent 600 micrometre/75% guideline is largely leporine and not an established clinical optimum.

verification: The review does not verify an original process, specimen, or model; manufacturing percentages and histomorphometric values are reported from cited studies (S003:C01; S008:C01-S008:C02).
calibration: No cross-study calibration of pore measurement, histology segmentation, animal defect size, or mechanical test is provided; review tables retain each study's conditions (S006:C01; S008:C01).
validation: Published in-vivo histology/histomorphometry provides secondary evidence about osseointegration, but species, anatomy, processing, and timing prevent direct validation of one universal lattice rule (S006:C01; S009:C01).
sensitivity: Qualitative sensitivity to pore size, porosity, strut size, topology, location, species, and time is discussed; no formal pooled sensitivity analysis or standardized dose-response model is performed (S005:C01; S009:C01).
application_prediction: The review suggests 300-600 micrometre pores, 50-70% porosity, and approximately 600 micrometre pores/75% porosity as conditional design directions, but these are application recommendations derived mainly from heterogeneous animal evidence (S007:C02; S010:C01).

primary_outcomes: Among reviewed in-vivo porous implants, approximately 98% used powder-bed processes (78% SLM, 12% EBM, 5% SLS, 3% DMLS) and most materials were Ti-6Al-4V (53%) or commercially pure titanium (44%); the remaining 3% included tantalum or iron-manganese (S003:C01).
Reviewed pore sizes span 50-1200 micrometres, strut thickness 120-800 micrometres, and porosity 30-83.5%; the review states that processing and topology are difficult to isolate (S005:C01).

Fibrous tissue can enter lattices at high porosity and ~600 micrometre pores, and exterior fibrosis can reduce BIC even when interior trabecular bone is healthy; woven bone generally precedes lamellar bone, with maturation delayed in high-porosity leporine implants (S007:C01-S007:C02).

Histomorphometry is commonly reported as BV/TV, BA, BIC, pull-out, push-out, or removal torque, but inner/outer region segmentation is inconsistent and larger-mammal interiors can show substantially less bone penetration than exteriors (S008:C01).

The review observes favorable but conflicting pore-size trends: many studies cluster around 300-600 micrometres, while canine data favor different sizes for penetration depth, bone area, or trabecular thickness; unit-cell architecture effects are also contradictory (S009:C01).

The review concludes that 50-70% porosity often shows reasonable osseointegration, 400-600 micrometre reticulated lattices at 60-70% porosity are most commonly studied, and an approximate 600 micrometre/75% combination is associated with early fibrovascular tissue and maturation largely from leporine data (S010:C01).
study.highest_evidence_level_reached: Heterogeneous secondary synthesis of preclinical in-vivo histology and histomorphometry; no standardized cross-species comparison, pooled effect estimate, original experiment, or clinical validation of an optimum lattice is reached.

argument_map.central_claim: In-vivo response to additively manufactured metallic lattices is conditional on topology, pore/strut geometry, porosity, material/process state, species, site, and time; current evidence supports design ranges and measurement practices, not a universal optimum.
data: Fabrication and material frequencies show that the evidence base is dominated by SLM titanium lattices, not by a balanced comparison of materials or processes (S003:C01).
Histological observations link fibrosis, strain, woven-to-lamellar maturation, porosity, and animal model to the quality and location of bone apposition (S007:C01-S007:C02).

Tables of BV/TV, BA, BIC, pull-out, and push-out values show strong dependence on pore size, porosity, species, time, and region segmentation, with contradictory architecture trends (S008:C01-S008:C02; S009:C01).
argument_map.warrant: A lattice recommendation is defensible only when geometry, material/process state, animal/site, time, histomorphometric region, and fixation proxy are matched; a study-count direction or one pore-size range cannot substitute for that comparability.
backing: The review explicitly states that direct quantitative comparison between species is unsuitable and that systematic in-vivo design studies are scarce (S006:C01; S008:C01).
Conflicting canine, leporine, and unit-cell findings show that bone quantity and quality can favor different designs (S009:C01).
argument_map.qualifier: Evidence map for preclinical osseointegration and osteoconduction; the proposed pore/porosity ranges are conditional heuristics, not clinical efficacy thresholds.
rebuttals_or_boundaries: The packet gives no reproducible search strategy, inclusion criteria, risk-of-bias assessment, or study-level denominator, so selection and publication bias are not auditable.
Histological maturity and BIC/BA/BV/TV are proxies whose relationship to load-bearing fixation, fatigue, revision, and patient function varies by model and interface.
Most reviewed implants are as-fabricated laboratory specimens; surface powder, anisotropy, heat treatment, and sterilization effects are not uniformly reported.
A 600 micrometre/75% design direction is dominated by leporine observations and cannot be generalized across species or human implant dimensions.

measured: The review reports measurements made in cited studies: pore/strut/porosity values, fabrication proportions, histology, BV/TV, BA, BIC, pull-out/push-out/removal-torque proxies, and time-specific maturation findings (S003:C01; S007:C01-S009:C01).
The review itself makes no new biological or mechanical measurements and the table values retain the original species, implant, region, and endpoint conditions.
predicted: Mechanics and transport discussions predict how porosity, strut frequency, unit-cell size, and curvature may alter stiffness, buckling, microfluidics, and strain; these are model or design interpretations rather than measured clinical outcomes (S004:C01-S005:C01).
A proposed strain threshold below 5% for intramembranous ossification is attributed to fracture-healing literature and is not a validated universal lattice threshold (S007:C01).
inferred: Pore size is inferred to influence mechanical anchorage while porosity is inferred to correlate more with maturation, but the variables are confounded by unit-cell, processing, species, and implantation-time differences (S009:C01-S010:C01).
Interior bone penetration and lamellar maturity are interpreted as indicators of long-term integration, yet the bridge to human load-bearing durability is not directly tested (S007:C01; S008:C01).
A 600 micrometre pore and 75% porosity combination is inferred to balance fibrovascular entry and maturation, mainly from leporine data (S007:C02; S010:C01).
recommended: Use a standardized, condition-matched matrix for pore size, strut/unit-cell design, porosity, material/process state, animal/site, region segmentation, implantation time, and fixation proxy.
Report both inner and outer lattice outcomes, bone quality/maturity, and mechanical fixation rather than a single bulk BIC or BA value (S008:C01).

Run cross-species and larger-implant studies with as-built geometry, surface state, fatigue, transport, and patient-relevant interface endpoints before clinical optimization (S005:C01; S006:C01; S010:C01).
proxy_to_outcome_bridges: BIC, BA, BV/TV, pull-out, push-out, and removal torque quantify local anchorage or bone amount; they do not by themselves establish functional fixation, fatigue durability, revision, or patient outcome (S008:C01).
Woven-to-lamellar histology and osteocyte density indicate maturation state but are not equivalent to mechanical quality under human loading (S007:C01-S007:C02).
Animal pore-size/porosity trends and critical-sized defects are preclinical proxies; species-specific bone structure and scaling limit clinical extrapolation (S006:C01; S010:C01).
overclaim_risks: The review's common 400-600 micrometre/60-70% values can be misread as an established optimum, although the review states that no optimum architecture is identified (S005:C01; S010:C01).
A strain threshold or lamellar-bone trend can be compressed into a universal mechanobiological rule without accounting for species, site, time, and material state (S007:C01-S007:C02).
Higher BIC or pull-out in one model does not establish superior clinical osseointegration, subsidence resistance, or long-term implant survival.

section_moves.move: Frame the review around biological response rather than manufacturing novelty
section_moves.execution: The introduction distinguishes earlier materials/mechanics reviews from this review's focus on in-vivo bone structure and quantitative histomorphometry (S002:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: State the evidence layer a review adds and do not let a technology label stand in for a biological endpoint.
section_moves.failure_mode: Calling an AM process clinically superior because it permits complex geometry bypasses the need for as-built and in-vivo evidence.

section_moves.move: Separate process, topology, and animal-model sources of variation
section_moves.execution: Fabrication methods, reticulated/stochastic/graded/TPMS structures, unit-cell modulation, and species/defect-size choices are described as distinct determinants before histology is compared (S003:C01-S006:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Make a comparator matrix before synthesizing a geometry effect when processing and biology vary together.
section_moves.failure_mode: Attributing a cross-study trend to pore size alone hides process, material, species, site, and time confounding.

section_moves.move: Pair histology time course with region-specific quantitative endpoints
section_moves.execution: The review links woven/lamellar maturation and fibrosis to BIC, BA, BV/TV, and pull/push-out measures while warning that inner/outer segmentation is inconsistent (S007:C01-S008:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Report tissue quality, location, time, and mechanical proxy together instead of treating one histomorphometric percentage as total integration.
section_moves.failure_mode: Bulk BIC or BA can conceal an exterior shell of bone and poor interior penetration in a large implant.

section_moves.move: Give conditional ranges and retain the missing optimum
section_moves.execution: The conclusion identifies common reticulated 400-600 micrometre/60-70% designs and a leporine-derived 600 micrometre/75% direction, then explicitly states that no topology is proven best and calls for systematic surface/architecture work (S010:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: When evidence supports a design neighborhood but not an optimum, report the neighborhood, its provenance, and the discriminating experiment still needed.
section_moves.failure_mode: Turning a common parameter range into a clinical prescription erases uncertainty and model dependence.

author_reported: The review emphasizes substantial inter-study variability, unsuitable direct cross-species quantitative comparison, inconsistent histomorphometric segmentation, and a lack of systematic evaluation of lattice designs (S006:C01; S008:C01; S010:C01).
Anisotropy and many surface-modification effects are outside the biological synthesis or underrepresented in-vivo evidence (S003:C01; S010:C01).
The 600 micrometre/75% balance is acknowledged to derive largely from leporine histology (S007:C02).
reader_identified: No database search string, screening flow, inclusion criteria, study-level risk-of-bias assessment, or denominator for included experiments is present in the packet.
Tables combine species, sites, materials, pore measurement conventions, implantation times, and region segmentation without a standardized uncertainty or meta-analytic model.
As-built geometry, surface powder, heat treatment, sterilization, fatigue, and interface loading are not consistently available across reviewed studies.
The review cannot determine whether commonly studied reticulated titanium reflects efficacy or simply equipment and publication availability.
likely_bias_direction: A citation-based review may overrepresent accessible titanium/SLM studies and underrepresent null, failed, or unpublished architectures.
Small-animal, short-term, exterior-biased sampling may overestimate interior osseointegration and maturation relative to human implants.
Reporting pore-size or porosity trends without full process and species context may overstate independent geometry effects.
limitations.scope_boundary: This review supports a preclinical evidence map for porous metallic implant histology and histomorphometry. It does not establish a universal pore architecture, human osseointegration threshold, subsidence/fatigue benefit, or clinical survival advantage.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: For an in-vivo lattice review, build a comparator matrix across process, material state, topology, pore/strut geometry, porosity, species/site, implantation time, tissue region, and fixation proxy before stating a design trend.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Review Methods, evidence table, Results synthesis, and audit.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: A pore-size trend that changes with canine geometry or leporine timing is not a geometry-only effect and cannot define a universal optimum.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Pair woven-to-lamellar histology and inner/outer spatial sampling with BIC/BA/BV/TV and pull/push-out proxies, explicitly separating bone quality from fixation and clinical function.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Histology Results, endpoint-vector tables, and translational Discussion.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: High exterior BIC or mature lamellae may coexist with poor interior penetration and does not establish human load-bearing durability.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Present a parameter neighborhood with provenance and uncertainty when the literature has common ranges but no controlled optimum.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Design recommendations, review conclusion, and future-study agenda.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: The 600 micrometre/75% suggestion is largely leporine and cannot be presented as a clinical prescription or universal mechanobiological threshold.

critical_weaknesses: No reproducible search, screening, or risk-of-bias protocol is reported.
Heterogeneous species, sites, material states, segmentation, and endpoint definitions prevent quantitative pooling.
No clinical, fatigue, or direct interface-durability validation of the proposed geometry ranges.

summary_zh: 这是一篇基于体内组织学/组织形态计量的叙述性综述，不是新动物实验。综述显示文献主要使用SLM制备的钛/ Ti-6Al-4V晶格，孔径约50–1200 μm、孔隙率30–83.5%，但物种、部位、时间、加工状态和内外区域分割差异很大。纤维包裹、编织骨到板层骨成熟、内外骨渗入梯度与BIC/BA/BV/TV/拉出/推出等代理终点必须分开解释；300–600 μm以及约600 μm/75%更多是条件性、以兔模型为主的设计邻域，不能当作临床最优或沉降/疲劳收益。
reader_notes: Primary Luna reader read every non-reference packet chunk in heading order: S001:C01 through S012:C01, including S004:C02, S007:C02, S008:C02, contribution, and conflict chunks.
Full text supports a narrative review with quantitative evidence tables; the metadata design cues are navigation only and do not imply original in-vivo experiments.
All values in the overlay are review-reported measurements from cited studies, with species/site/time and proxy boundaries retained.
No references chunk was present and no substantive non-reference locator was omitted.
